name: MathlibAnnex.Sphere.radialExtension_leftInverse
title: The inverse sphere isometry gives the inverse radial map

content.display_title: The inverse sphere isometry gives the inverse radial map
content.one_sentence_role: Shows that extending the inverse sphere isometry radially undoes the forward radial extension.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $X,Y$ be real normed spaces and $\Delta:S_X\to S_Y$ a bijective isometry for the ambient chord metrics. Here $S_X=\{u\in X:\|u\|=1\}$ and $S_Y=\{v\in Y:\|v\|=1\}$ are the unit spheres. Write $R_\Delta(0)=0$ and $R_\Delta(x)=\|x\|\Delta(x/\|x\|)$ for $x\ne0$, and define $R_{\Delta^{-1}}$ in the same way. Then

$$R_{\Delta^{-1}}(R_\Delta(x))=x\qquad(x\in X).$$
content.assumptions: The only geometric assumptions are that $X,Y$ are real normed spaces and $\Delta$ is a bijective isometry between their unit spheres. The inverse used here is the inverse of that same $\Delta$. Completeness, finite-dimensionality and a positive dimension are not required.
content.conclusion: The map $R_{\Delta^{-1}}$ is a left inverse of $R_\Delta$. Applying this result to $\Delta^{-1}$ gives $R_\Delta(R_{\Delta^{-1}}(y))=y$ for all $y\in Y$, recorded separately as the right-inverse theorem. The two radial maps therefore give a bijection of the ambient spaces.
content.proof_summary:
For $x=0$ both maps give zero. For $x\ne0$, set $r=\|x\|>0$, $u=x/r$ and $y=R_\Delta(x)=r\Delta(u)$. Since $\Delta(u)\in S_Y$, norm preservation gives $\|y\|=r>0$, so $y\ne0$ and $y/\|y\|=\Delta(u)$. Substitution into the inverse radial formula gives

$$R_{\Delta^{-1}}(y)=r\Delta^{-1}(\Delta(u))=ru=x.$$

The cancellation uses the inverse of the given sphere equivalence, and positive normalization makes the argument of that inverse exactly $\Delta(u)$.

proof_steps.text: For $x\ne0$, the norm identity rules out $R_\Delta(x)=0$. Thus the nonzero branch of the inverse radial definition is applicable.
Normalize $r\Delta(u)$ using $r>0$ and $\|\Delta(u)\|=1$. Its unit direction is $\Delta(u)$, so the inverse sphere map returns $u$, and multiplication by the preserved radius returns $x$.

content.lean_realization_notes: Bundling these two maps as `radialExtensionEquiv` uses precisely these inverse identities. The later homeomorphism uses the same maps with continuity proofs. Neither bundling chooses a new map.
